title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. The page studies 'liftings' u of an automorphism, with cyclotomic character p = χ(u) ∈ Ẑ*, acting on the profinite fundamental group π̂_{0,3} of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. The ambient group is the extended Teichmüller group Γ̂^+_{0,3}, generated by π̂_{0,3} together with σ_∞ (order 2, fixes ∞ and swaps 0 and 1) and ρ (order 3, cyclically permutes 0, 1, ∞). The loops are l_0, l_1 around 0 and 1, and L_0 is the closed subgroup generated by l_0.

As the previous page explains, u is encoded by a 'path' g_0 ∈ π̂_{0,3}/L_0 and by g ∈ π̂_{0,3}. Here g is the element such that g·ρ is the image of ρ, and it must satisfy condition (51): gρ has order 3, i.e. g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = 1.

Step (60). Since p ∈ Ẑ* is odd, Grothendieck sets γ = (p−1)/2 ∈ Ẑ. This is exactly Drinfeld's m = (λ−1)/2.

Step (61). He sets h_0 = g_0^{-1} σ_∞(g_0), the 'coboundary' of g_0 with respect to the involution σ_∞. He notes explicitly that this inverts his earlier convention.

Step (62). The compatibility conditions (54) force g to be expressed through g_0 and γ:
  g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^γ ρ(g_0)^{-1} = λ ξ ρ(λ)^{-1},
with λ = g_0 l_0^{-γ} and ξ = l_0^γ h_0. The second equality uses ρ(l_0) = l_1 and is correct.

Step (63)–(64). The u are therefore parametrized by pairs (g_0, γ) with 2γ+1 ∈ Ẑ* and condition (51). Because g is a twisted conjugate of ξ, we get
  g ρ(g) ρ²(g) = λ ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) λ^{-1}  (using ρ³ = 1).
Hence (51) is equivalent to the boxed relation
  ξ ρ(ξ) ρ²(ξ) = 1, with ξ = l_0^γ g_0^{-1} σ_∞(g_0).

Identification. With f = h_0 and m = γ, this is precisely Drinfeld's hexagon ('3-cycle') relation for elements (λ, f) of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group: f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1 with xyz = 1, m = (λ−1)/2. The next page adds σ_∞(h_0) h_0 = 1, which is the 2-cycle relation f(x,y) f(y,x) = 1. So this page is Grothendieck's own derivation of the GT^ defining relations (I) and (II). They arise as the conditions for an automorphism of π̂_{0,3} to extend compatibly to the order-2 and order-3 symmetries of the tripod. Notably, f appears as a σ_∞-coboundary of a path g_0 from the tangential base point at 0.

The left margin explains the notation: h_0 is to the involution σ_∞ of order 2 what g is to the automorphism ρ of order 3. The other margin notes record that the expression for g follows by the change g_0 ↦ g_0 l_0^{-γ}, and that the convention for h_0 was inverted.
errors: No mathematical error found. The identity (62)=λξρ(λ)^{-1} holds provided ρ(l_0)=l_1 (and σ_∞(l_0)=l_1), which matches Grothendieck's conventions.
The equivalence (51)⇔(64) is a correct twisted-conjugation argument.
The next page assumes, without proof, that π̂_{0,3}^{σ_∞}={1} and that h_0 is a σ_∞-coboundary iff σ_∞(h_0)h_0=1. He flags these explicitly as 'admis provisoirement'; this is a gap, not an error.

ideas.what: Parameter γ=(p−1)/2 attached to the cyclotomic character p∈Ẑ*, entering as l_0^γ in the 3-cycle relation
ideas.modern_name: m=(λ−1)/2 in the definition of the profinite Grothendieck–Teichmüller group GT^
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990, 'On quasitriangular quasi-Hopf algebras and a group closely connected with Gal(Q̄/Q)'); Ihara (1990-91) for the Galois side
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only announces that Gal acts on the Teichmüller tower determined by levels 1 and 2 (genus 0 with 3/4 points); no explicit equations

ideas.what: Writing the GT element as h_0=g_0^{-1}σ_∞(g_0), a σ_∞-coboundary of a path g_0 modulo L_0
ideas.modern_name: f(x,y) as the image of the 'droit chemin' from 0 to 1 (Ihara's f_σ; Drinfeld associator as the path from 01 to 10)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara; Deligne (1989, tangential base points); Drinfeld

ideas.what: Hexagon relation ξρ(ξ)ρ²(ξ)=1 with ξ=l_0^γ h_0, derived from the requirement that ρ (order 3) lifts to an order-3 element

ideas.modern_name: nonabelian H^1 / twisted conjugacy for Z/3

missed.claim: Grothendieck writes down, independently of and probably before Drinfeld (1990), the hexagonal defining relation of GT^ in the exact form with m=(λ−1)/2. He derives it conceptually from the order-3 symmetry ρ of the tripod and the involution σ_∞. This is a group-theoretic derivation (extension of the action to Γ̂^+_{0,3}) rather than via quasi-Hopf algebras. Combined with the next page, both relations (I) and (II) appear.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point: the literature generally credits the GT equations to Drinfeld (with Ihara). It is said that Grothendieck 'envisioned' GT, but not that he wrote down the equations explicitly. The derivation also gives a clean 'symmetry-lifting' interpretation of the relations, with g_0 as a path and f as its σ_∞-coboundary.

missed.claim: The two admitted facts are left provisional on the next page: π̂_{0,3}^{σ_∞}=1, and that coboundaries are exactly the h with σ_∞(h)h=1. The parametrization of the u by (ζ,γ) also depends on the two conjugacy classes of order-3 lifts (p≡±1 mod 3).
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: These are nonabelian cohomology statements for Z/2 acting on the profinite free group. The p≡±1 (mod 3) dichotomy for the two order-3 conjugacy classes is a fine point rarely made explicit in GT literature.

deep.surprise_reason: An explicit, correct derivation of the Drinfeld/Ihara GT^ hexagon relation (with m=(λ−1)/2), in Grothendieck's hand, in notes apparently predating Drinfeld. Specialists know Grothendieck anticipated GT in spirit, and the archive's 'équation des lacets' notes have begun to be studied (e.g. by Schneps), so this is not entirely unknown. Still, the exact equations and the coboundary formulation are a notable unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'la situation a connu considérablement' is likely 'la situation se complique considérablement'.
The conditions referred to on the first lines appear to be '(54)', not '(59)'. Likewise '(équivalente à (54) (iv) ou (v))'.

Left margin likely reads: 'h_0 relatif à l'automorphisme σ_∞ d'ordre 2, vu son rôle analogue à g relatif à l'automorphisme ρ d'ordre 3 – ceci motivait le changement des notations plus haut' (approximate).
Lower-left margin: 'NB cette expression de g suit par changement g_0 ↦ g_0 l_0^{-γ}' rather than 'g_0 ↦ g_0 l_0'.
Right margin: 'NB On appelle ici h_0 ce que précédemment on notait h_0^{-1}'.
